payload.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=methods+for+cross-model+verification+of+foundational+premises+in+reasoning+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6654038\", \"title\": [\"FRFP Lean Formal Verification: A Machine-Checked Companion to the Foundational Reasoning and Feedback Protocol\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>We present a complete machine-checked formalization of the Foundational Reasoning and Feedback Protocol (FRFP) using the Lean 4 proof assistant. Starting from the published FRFP theory, we formalize 21 modules comprising 269 verified theorems and 155 fully cited axioms, with zero outstanding sorry placeholders and zero uncited assumptions. Beyond confirming existing claims, the formalization shows that the original 11-axiom basis reduces to 7 independent primitives, with 4 former axioms derivable as theorems from the remaining core. Three non-trivial results emerge directly from Lean proof obligations: a canonical earliest-unresolved-witness theorem, a governance-safe trace-extension theorem, and a protocol normal-form decomposition theorem. We describe the AI-assisted development methodology (vibecoding), characterize observed failure modes and success rates, and provide a complete reproducibility package.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6654038\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006\", \"title\": [\"Axioms and foundational premises\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2014, 1, 30]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-3-319-47166-2_3\", \"title\": [\"Survey of Statistical Verification of Linear Unbounded Properties: Model Checking and Distances\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-47166-2_3\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2016]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-1-4757-3188-0_9\", \"title\": [\"Verification of a Simple Pipelined Machine Model\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4757-3188-0_9\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2000]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "7ac0565b6325bb666434608bc2c02573054c5a0c404ff852c73797fe46b37cf3", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6654038", "doi:10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006", "doi:10.1007/978-3-319-47166-2_3", "doi:10.1007/978-1-4757-3188-0_9"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6654038", "https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006", "https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-47166-2_3", "https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4757-3188-0_9"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
